stories.title: LS Electric, GE Vernova to form JV on high-voltage direct current projects
stories.summary: South Korean power equipment maker LS Electric Co. said Wednesday it will form a joint venture with U.S. energy technology company GE Vernova to cooperate in the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) sector. The two companies signed an agreement to establish the joint venture, tentatively named "Grid X Technology," on the sidelines of the CIGRE 2026 Session in Paris on Tuesday (local time). Under the agreement, the two companies will collaborate on South Korea's voltage source converter (VSC)-based HVDC projects, a key part of the country's efforts to transmit electricity generated from renewable energy sources in the southwestern region to the densely populated Seoul metropolitan area. The joint venture will combine the two companies' technologies and expertise to develop HVDC solutions and establish strategies for the stable supply of key components and equipment, with the aim to enter the global HVDC market. GE Vernova is a U.S.-based global energy technology and power infrastructure company spun off from General Electric (GE) in April 2024.

stories.title: Minor party leader resigns to take responsibility for local election defeat
stories.summary: The leader of the minor opposition New Reform Party stepped down Wednesday to take responsibility for the party's defeat in the June 3 local elections. Lee Jun-seok announced the decision during a press conference at the National Assembly, saying he had made several proposals to reform the party since the elections but failed to gain sufficient support from within. "This is no one's fault," he said. "The responsibility for failing to persuade others lies entirely with me as the party leader." The minor party failed to win any of the 16 major mayoral and gubernatorial posts or the 14 parliamentary seats up for grabs in the June 3 elections, winning just one local council seat. The party fell into further disarray when one of its candidates, Jeong Yi-han, was arrested and indicted on charges of staging an assault on himself, in an apparent attempt to woo voters ahead of the elections. Chun Ha-ram, the party's floor leader, is expected to serve as acting party leader following Lee's resignation.

stories.title: In Australia, Disney’s Ooshies send Woolworths whooshing ahead of Coles
stories.summary: Ooshies were not just fun to collect – the tiny plastic Disney figurines were powerful enough to move sales between Australia’s supermarket giants. Woolworths Group said on Wednesday that Australian food sales jumped 7.6 per cent in the first eight weeks of the 2027 financial year, with its Ooshies promotion contributing an estimated 1.5 to 2 percentage points of growth.
